title: Mitigation & Preparation
welcome_lead: Compare DRR strategies in Japan and Philippines.

final_note: Preparation transforms hazard into manageable risk.

walkthroughs.body_html: EEW system gives 8-30 seconds warning via TV, mobile, trains. Tokyo SkyTree 634 m uses oil dampers + central concrete core. Bosai Day (1 September) drills since 1960. School-based education from age 5. Tsunami sea walls up to 15 m post-2011. Cost: $1.5 billion/yr DRR investment.

Typhoon Haiyan November 2013 Cat 5: 6300 deaths, 16 million affected. Pre-event PAGASA forecasts accurate but evacuation slow; storm surge 7 m at Tacloban. Post: Build Back Better with stronger schools (each typhoon-rated). Bangsamoro Disaster Risk Reduction Office established 2018.

Sendai 2015-2030 sets 7 global targets including reducing global disaster mortality. ODA for DRR reached $4.9 billion in 2020 but still <0.5 percent of total. UNDRR Words Into Action guidelines support implementation. Challenge: integrate climate adaptation with DRR.

mcqs.q: What is the difference between mitigation and adaptation to climate change?
options: Mitigation is done by HICs and adaptation is done by LICs.
A hazard happens on land and a disaster happens at sea.
Mitigation reduces the causes (cutting greenhouse gas emissions); adaptation reduces the impacts (e.g. building sea walls, drought-resistant crops, early warning systems).
Mitigation and adaptation mean the same thing — both are about stopping climate change.

mcqs.q: What is the difference between the Burgess and Hoyt urban land use models?
options: Burgess and Hoyt models show the same thing in different drawings.
Burgess (1925) describes concentric rings radiating from the CBD; Hoyt (1939) describes sectors (wedges) extending along transport routes — recognising how transport shapes urban growth.
A hazard happens on land and a disaster happens at sea.
Burgess is for American cities and Hoyt is for European cities.

mcqs.q: What is the difference between a natural hazard and a natural disaster?
options: A hazard happens on land and a disaster happens at sea.
They are the same thing — any earthquake or hurricane is a disaster.
A natural hazard is a physical event with potential to cause harm; it becomes a disaster only when it affects vulnerable people and causes significant impact.
Mitigation is done by HICs and adaptation is done by LICs.
